t: You're looking at a white marble statue of Queen Victoria, set on a Portland stone base near Kensington Palace. It shows her at eighteen, seated in her coronation robes, and it resembles the painting of her coronation by Sir George Hayter. It was put up in 1893, and the sculptor was her own daughter, Princess Louise, Duchess of Argyll, Victoria's fourth daughter. So this is a mother portrayed by her child. Victoria reigned from 1837 to 1901, longer than any monarch before her, and gave her name to an age. The statue has been Grade II listed since 1969.
